title_en: MacroVoices #551 Michael Every: Decoding The Global Geopolitical Puzzle (Part 2)
title_zh: MacroVoices #551 Michael Every：解读全球地缘政治拼图（下）
subtitle_zh: Michael Every 深入分析美中冷战格局下的地缘政治、能源武器化与 AI 军备竞赛风险
summary_zh: 本期是 MacroVoices 首期「MacroVoices Unplugged」加时节目，主持 Eric Townsend 与 Rabobank 全球策略师 Michael Every 延续前一日的第 551 期访谈，因内容太多而额外录制。Townsend 坦承本期放宽了编辑标准、允许探讨推测性理论（而非阴谋论），试图串联遍地开花的未经证实传闻，且核心线索都指向中国：南海事件、朝鲜据报测试高超音速武器（hypersonic weapons）、以及习近平可能计划以武力统一台湾。Every 分析 Axios 报道的伊朗对美一周最后通牒（解除军事封锁否则恢复非对称升级），以及沙特冒险经霍尔木兹海峡（Strait of Hormuz）增运石油、伊朗威胁把打击扩展到曼德海峡（Bab el-Mandeb）、红海乃至印度洋船对船转运的风险。节目还谈及 Politico 报道的 Trump 至少 90 天柴油出口禁令、格陵兰风波，以及美中「冷战」格局下美国再工业化、再军事化对加拿大等盟友的诉求、稀土（rare earths）胁迫与 AI 军备竞赛——包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 本地气隔（air gap）部署优势，以及中国可能靠免费赠送来颠覆美国 AI 繁荣。Every 亦不排除俄罗斯在乌克兰动用战术核武器的尾部风险。

turns.en: Do you really think the U.S. is going to accept a Canada which drifts away from it geopolitically, starts doing deals with China, maybe, or with Europe, and then who knows where Europe goes in the future, and have a long, open, undefended border with it?

turns.zh: 你会想先听第一部分，所以如果你不小心找到了这里——因为它排在播放列表最前面——请先去听第一部分。

turns.zh: 你可以在 Macro Voices 第551期找到它，于9月24日发布。现在，在和 Michael 继续深入之前，我要借此机会告诉你，根据你们在 X 和其他平台上的反馈，我们将开始尝试这种新形式。

turns.zh: 我们坚定承诺将旗舰播客中的专题访谈保持在45到50分钟的目标时长。这一点不会改变，这是出于对你们时间的尊重。

turns.zh: 未来的变化是，当我们有像 Michael 这样的嘉宾，显然有更多话要说而不是分配的时间能容纳的，我们会在事后录制一期加时节目。

turns.en: That's what we're doing now one day later. I'm going to ask for your patience, especially on this inaugural overtime episode, because we hit our production team up with this at the 11th hour.
turns.zh: 这就是我们现在在一天后做的事情。我要请求你们的耐心，特别是在这首期加时节目中，因为我们在最后一刻才把这个任务交给制作团队。

turns.en: We don't have a budget for this. We didn't have a plan for this, and so we're going to relax our editing standards. Please bear with us. You'll probably hear a few editing glitches on this one, because we asked our team to put it out really quickly in order to get the content to you.
turns.zh: 我们没有为此编列预算，也没有为此制定计划，所以我们要放松编辑标准。请耐心包涵。你们可能会听到一些剪辑上的小问题，因为我们要求团队非常快地发布，以便把内容传递给你们。

turns.en: Don't expect this every week. We're going to experiment it for special guests like Michael, Anasalhaji, people who have so much to say that it doesn't fit in an hour.

turns.en: Michael, let's dive in. Well, wait a minute. I was going to say where we left off on part one, but so much news has happened in the last 24 hours since we recorded part one that I want to just dive into what's happened since then.
turns.zh: Michael，让我们开始吧。等等，我本来要说我们从第一部分中断的地方继续，但自从我们录制第一部分以来的24小时内发生了太多新闻，我想直接进入此后发生的事情。

turns.en: I want to reset our ground rules a little bit. Let's call this macro voices unplugged that we're doing this extra session here. I'm going to say let's just say normally we try to avoid unconfirmed rumors and speculative theories.
turns.zh: 我想稍微重新设定我们的基本规则。就把我们这次额外的环节叫做 Macro Voices Unplugged 吧。我要说，通常我们尽量避免未经证实的传闻和推测性理论。

turns.en: Let's say they're fair game because, frankly, last time we avoided those, neither one of us could figure out what the heck is going on in the world because it's a complicated picture.
turns.zh: 但这次我们就把它们当作合理话题吧，因为坦率地说，上次我们回避了那些，结果我们俩都搞不清这个世界到底怎么了，因为局势太复杂了。

turns.en: Let's just say it's okay to go into speculative theories, not quite conspiracy theories, but let's not apologize for questioning the mainstream narrative and try to figure out what the hell is really going on here as we might do in private conversation.
turns.zh: 我们就说可以探讨推测性理论吧——不是阴谋论——但我们不必为质疑主流叙事而道歉，试着像我们在私下对话中那样搞清楚这里到底发生了什么。

turns.en: As I alluded at the end of part one, boy, unverified rumors are a target-rich environment right now. Between the South China Sea incidents, North Korea reportedly testing hypersonic weapons, Xi Jinping's possible designs on invading Taiwan as part of a campaign to repatriate Taiwan as part of the People's Republic of China.
turns.zh: 正如我在第一部分末尾提到的，天哪，未经证实的传闻现在简直是遍地开花。南海事件、朝鲜据报测试高超音速武器（hypersonic weapons）、习近平可能计划入侵台湾——作为将台湾回归中华人民共和国的一部分。

turns.en: There's no shortage of topics to fill this bonus session before we just got hit this morning with three more news items. So I'll come back to those things and I really want to connect the dots because I think they all connect back to China somehow.
turns.zh: 话题多的是，足以填满这期加时节目。而且今天早上我们又收到了三条新消息。所以我稍后会回到那些话题，我真的很想把线索串联起来，因为我认为它们都以某种方式与中国有关。

turns.en: I just haven't quite figured it out. Let's start with the three stories that have happened. The first one, according to Ola Hansen, our good friend over at Saxo Bank, Axios reporting this morning that Iran has essentially given the United States a one-week ultimatum to either lift the military blockade or they will resume asymmetric escalations.
turns.zh: 只是我还没完全想通。让我们从已经发生的三个故事开始。第一个，根据我们的好朋友、Saxo Bank 的 Ole Hansen 所说，Axios 今早报道伊朗基本上给了美国一周的最后通牒——要么解除军事封锁，要么他们将恢复非对称升级行动。

turns.en: That spiked crude oil this morning, I'm only looking at WTI, I don't have a Brent chart in front of me, but that first spike was a good $3.5 just on that news.
turns.zh: 今早原油价格因此飙升。我只在看 WTI，面前没有 Brent 的图表，但仅这条消息第一波飙升就有大约3.5美元。

turns.en: It seems to me like this was kind of predictable. What do you think, Michael? It was predictable because you are also seeing stories at the same time that actually the Saudis are starting to follow the UAE's lead and have been successfully shuttling more and more oil through Hormuz, which of course is still seeing live firing, it's still seeing the odd shit being hit.
turns.zh: 在我看来这似乎是可预见的。你怎么看，Michael？这是可预见的，因为你同时也看到这样的报道——沙特实际上开始跟随阿联酋的步伐，成功地通过霍尔木兹海峡（Strait of Hormuz）运送越来越多的石油。当然那里仍有实弹射击，仍偶尔有船只被击中。

turns.en: And yet with the pressing importance of trying to get that crude flow going, the Saudis have been prepared to go ahead with it anyway, which just means that oil is that much more expensive from a security perspective.
turns.zh: 然而，鉴于恢复原油流通的紧迫重要性，沙特人一直准备无论如何都要推进，这意味着从安全角度来看，石油的成本更加高昂了。

turns.en: The cost involved in getting it out and insurance, et cetera, et cetera, but it can still flow. But Iran was never just going to sit there, this is an economic war and a physical war at the same time and say, oh, well, you've foxed me there, there's nothing I can do.
turns.zh: 把它运出来的成本、保险等等，但它仍然可以流通。但伊朗从来不会只是坐在那里——这是一场经济战争同时也是一场实体战争——然后说，哦，好吧，你把我将住了，我无能为力。

turns.en: So now they are saying, yeah, okay, whether there is a fixed deadline or not, we don't know. But the implication is that not only will they keep striking in Hormuz, not only can they escalate the way they already have via the Houthis in Babel Mandib and the Red Sea, but they're now talking about the Indian Ocean too.
turns.zh: 所以他们现在是在说，好吧，不管有没有确定的最后期限，我们不知道。但言下之意是，他们不仅会继续在霍尔木兹海峡发动打击，不仅可以通过他们已经在做的——利用曼德海峡（Bab el-Mandeb）和红海的胡塞武装（Houthis）来升级——而且他们现在还在谈论印度洋。

turns.en: Now whether they can or can't strike that far remains to be seen, but you wouldn't want to rule it out given that one of their missiles got as far as Cyprus at one point earlier on in the year, which would mean that you could potentially disrupt energy flows much further afield and more likely also hit those ship to ship transfers, which are happening off the coast of Omar, at which point, yes, not only do you have all the other problems we
turns.zh: 至于他们能不能打到那么远还有待观察，但你不能排除这种可能性——鉴于今年早些时候他们的一枚导弹曾打到塞浦路斯那么远。这意味着他们可能会在更远的地方扰乱能源流通，而且更可能打击那些在阿曼海岸外进行的船对船转运。到那时，是的，不仅会有我们已有的所有其他问题，

turns.en: have, you then have potentially lower crude flows too. We could probably do an interview on that alone, but let's go to the second of our three stories before we get into the full interview that we had planned.
turns.zh: 而且还可能出现更低的原油流量。我们可能就这一点单独做一期访谈，但让我们在进入原计划的完整访谈之前，先来看三个故事中的第二个。

turns.en: The number two story, Politico reporting that President Trump is apparently committed to at least a 90-day ban on export of diesel. And something I find really interesting is Energy Secretary Chris Wright has in the past just been almost the first word out of that guy's mouth is always under the leadership of President Trump.
turns.zh: 第二个故事，Politico 报道 Trump 总统似乎已承诺至少实施90天的柴油出口禁令。我觉得特别有意思的是，能源部长 Chris Wright 过去几乎张嘴第一句话总是「在 Trump 总统的领导下」。

turns.en: The most loyal and obedient subordinate in the president's entire world, and he's coming out on the public stage saying, no, that's a dumb idea, the markets don't work that way, let's not do that.
turns.zh: 他是总统整个世界中最忠诚、最服从的下属，而现在他公开站出来说，不，那是个愚蠢的主意，市场不是那样运作的，我们不应该那样做。

turns.en: So he's directly disagreeing with the president and it seems he's losing that fight. The president says, no, we're moving forward anyway with a 90-day ban on export of diesel fuel from the United States.
turns.zh: 所以他直接和总统意见相左，而且看起来他正在输掉这场争论。总统说，不，我们无论如何都要推进，对美国柴油出口实施90天禁令。

turns.en: I think most of our listeners already understand this, but very quickly, why don't you start with why that's probably not going to have the effect that President Trump is hoping for and then let's get into the background of why this is happening and why we're seeing, I think, a breakdown of trust between Secretary Wright and President Trump.
turns.zh: 我想我们大多数听众已经理解这一点了，但简单说一下——你为什么不先解释为什么这可能不会产生 Trump 总统所期望的效果，然后我们再谈谈这件事为什么会发生，以及为什么我们看到——我认为——Wright 部长和 Trump 总统之间的信任破裂。

turns.en: We discussed that in the first part, but just to reiterate, obviously in a complex, integrated global energy system in which different parts of the US interface with other countries and the whole world relies on counterparties.
turns.zh: 我们在第一部分讨论过这个，但我再重申一下。显然，在一个复杂的、一体化的全球能源系统中，美国的不同地区与其他国家对接，全世界都依赖交易对手（counterparties）。

turns.en: If you suddenly stop the US exporting diesel, it doesn't just solve one problem, it creates lots of others in equal measure, and the blowback can be more expensive crude, which of course then ends up with more expensive fuel prices anyway, and it can be shortages, obviously internationally and major geopolitical problems, but it can even be shortages and problems in the US.
turns.zh: 如果你突然停止美国出口柴油，它不只是解决一个问题，它同时会制造出很多其他问题。反弹可能是更昂贵的原油——当然这最终导致更贵的燃料价格——可能是短缺，显然是国际上的短缺和重大地缘政治问题，但也可能是美国国内的短缺和问题。

turns.en: But what I did say, and I would like to just reiterate again here for those who maybe didn't hear me say it the first time, is when you look at that particular nexus of problems and that network, it is operating on the basis that we do have that integrated one world global economy energy system, and I am still deeply cynical, but that is something that actually strengthens the US relative position vis-à-vis China, vis-à-vis others over the
turns.zh: 但我确实说过——我想在此再为那些可能没有听到我第一次说的人重申——当你审视那个特定的问题关联和那个网络时，它是在我们确实拥有一个一体化的全球世界经济能源系统的基础上运作的。我仍然对此深感怀疑，但从长期来看，这实际上增强了美国相对于中国、相对于其他国家的地位。

turns.en: longer term. It would not surprise me at all that if this 90-day ban does go through, which isn't confirmed yet, it's a political rumor, and it wouldn't surprise me at all if once it goes in, you get complete chaos and market meltdown in different locations, and then you see the thing refined, and they decide, well, okay, we're not going to do it against everybody, we're only going to do it against ABC or XYZ, and then gradually you get other supporting
turns.zh: 如果这个90天禁令确实通过了——目前还没有确认，这只是政治传闻——我一点也不会感到意外：一旦实施，你会在不同地方看到完全的混乱和市场崩溃，然后你会看到这个政策被修正，他们会决定，好吧，我们不会对所有国家都这样做，我们只对 ABC 或 XYZ 这样做。然后你会逐渐看到其他配套

turns.en: policies brought in as well. For example, as I said in refineries, to say you don't get to make a choice of what your refinery runs look like, or the government starts saying, well, we're going to pay for extra storage, so you can keep refining it, and we'll provide you with subsidized storage somewhere so that we can at least have an SPR for diesel, et cetera, et cetera, et cetera.
turns.zh: 政策也被引入。例如，就像我在炼油厂方面说的——你不能选择你的炼油厂运行什么样的产品；或者政府开始说，好吧，我们将为额外储存买单，这样你就可以继续炼油，我们会在某处为你提供补贴储存，这样我们至少可以为柴油建立一个战略石油储备（SPR），等等等等。

turns.en: So I think we're opening the door to all those kinds of things if we go ahead with them. But obviously, if you are a product of the private sector in the energy sector in the US, and you understand how it works, you would be opposed to that measure as a headline act.
turns.zh: 所以我认为如果我们推进这些措施，就是在为所有这类事情打开大门。但显然，如果你出身于美国能源行业的私营部门，了解它的运作方式，你会反对把这项措施作为一个标题性的行动。

turns.en: Well, it sounds like the setup from what you're saying is that we passed this 90-day rule. You end up cutting off nations whose ability to deliver food to their people literally depends on having diesel fuel.
turns.zh: 嗯，从你说的话来看，这个布局似乎是——我们通过了这个90天规则，然后你最终切断了那些其向人民交付粮食的能力实际上依赖柴油的国家。

turns.en: And then it sets the stage for the administration to say, oh, you don't like that, huh? Which world leader wants to kneel and beg first? And I'll consider on an individual basis issuing exemptions to this blanket ban.
turns.zh: 然后这就为政府搭好了舞台，让他们可以说，哦，你不喜欢这样是吧？哪个世界领导人想第一个跪下乞求？我会在个案基础上考虑发布这项全面禁令的豁免。

turns.en: I mean, is that what you're suggesting we could be heading toward? I don't think it will necessarily be done in quite such, excuse the pun, crude terms.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，这是你认为我们可能走向的方向吗？我不认为它会以如此——请原谅这个双关语——「粗糙」（crude）的方式实施。

turns.en: But I do think that's exactly the underlying dynamic, because if you have something that is vitally important to others, and they're not doing what you want them to do, economic coercion is a tool as old as time.
turns.zh: 但我确实认为这正是潜在的底层动态，因为如果你拥有对他人至关重要的东西，而他们没有按你的意愿行事，经济胁迫（economic coercion）是一种和时间一样古老的工具。

turns.en: It's certainly been used by lots of others. It's currently being used by lots of others at the moment. And most other countries that aren't doing it would do it if they had the ability to do it.
turns.zh: 它当然被很多其他国家使用过。目前很多其他国家正在使用它。而且大多数目前没有这样做的国家，如果有能力的话也会这样做。

turns.en: But when you are in a Cold War, a geopolitical clash with other countries, the very last thing you want to do is to turn around and say, what I always say flippantly, well, because markets, this is best for markets, markets are not necessarily best for national security.
turns.zh: 但当你处于冷战之中，与其他国家存在地缘政治冲突时，你最不想做的事情就是转身说——我总是半开玩笑地说——「因为市场，这对市场最好」。市场不一定对国家安全最有利。

turns.en: Now, neither is irritating everybody, neither is driving away your allies, neither is seeing people being plunged into poverty. There is a fine line between the two.
turns.zh: 当然，激怒所有人也不是对国家安全最有利，赶走你的盟友也不是，让人们陷入贫困也不是。两者之间有一条微妙的界线。

turns.en: And what I'm saying is, again, it wouldn't surprise me if this does happen. It wouldn't surprise me if we then have exactly that kind of negotiating process that you're talking about, but towards other goals.
turns.zh: 我要说的是，再一次，如果这真的发生了，我一点也不会感到意外。如果我们随后正好有了你所描述的那种谈判过程，我也不会感到意外——但目标是其他的。

turns.en: And one of them, I think, would be to make sure that those who the US works most closely with and trust the most are at the top of the priority list of fuel, and those who aren't or who refuse to kiss the ring are at the bottom of that list.
turns.zh: 其中之一，我认为，是确保那些与美国合作最密切、最受信任的国家排在燃料优先名单的顶端，而那些不合作的或拒绝「亲吻戒指」（kiss the ring）的国家排在名单的底部。

turns.en: And welcome to 2026 and 2027 and 2028, et cetera, et cetera. That's the way the world now works. Well, surely we can't really think that all of the news is going to go that badly.
turns.zh: 欢迎来到2026年、2027年和2028年等等等等。世界现在就是这样运作的。嗯，我们总不能真的认为所有新闻都会往那么坏的方向走吧。

turns.en: So let's move on to number three. Oh, wait a minute, maybe it can. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney apparently has directed the Canadian military to do war game simulations and so forth and to assess how Canada should respond if the US were to mount a full-scale military invasion on Canada.
turns.zh: 让我们继续看第三个。哦，等等，也许真会。加拿大总理 Mark Carney 显然已经指示加拿大军队进行战争模拟推演等，评估如果美国对加拿大发动全面军事入侵，加拿大应该如何应对。

turns.en: Did that really happen? I feel awkward even having set the rules for this, uh, macro voice is unplugged to say we're going to go ahead and do unconfirmed rumor.
turns.zh: 这真的发生了吗？我甚至为自己设定了这次「Macro Voices Unplugged」的规则——说我们要讨论未经证实的传闻——而感到尴尬。

turns.en: Are you sure that really happened and I wasn't dreaming it? It's in the Canadian press. It's in the New York Times and it's Mark Carney saying it, so I take it as read.
turns.zh: 你确定这真的发生了，不是我在做梦吗？这在加拿大媒体上有报道，New York Times 也有，而且是 Mark Carney 自己说的，所以我当作是真的。

turns.en: All I can say is, first of all, a little bit of history, when Canada was still under British Empire rule, they had a plan to invade the US. Of course they did.
turns.zh: 我只能说，首先讲一点历史。当加拿大还在大英帝国统治下时，他们有一个入侵美国的计划。他们当然有。

turns.en: It's very well known. You can Google it. During that particular era, like a hundred years ago, the US had a plan to invade Canada as well. This is well known.
turns.zh: 这是众所周知的，你可以 Google 搜到。在那个特定时代——大约一百年前——美国也有一个入侵加拿大的计划。这也是众所周知的。

turns.en: It's not new. It's just new in recent history and most militaries around the world do have, you know, what if scenarios in dusty desk drawers that they can pull out, you know, in wild situations.
turns.zh: 这不是什么新鲜事，只是在近代史上算新鲜。世界上大多数军队确实都有那种「如果……怎么办」的情景预案放在积灰的抽屉里，在极端情况下可以拿出来。

turns.en: So that's not a complete surprise and that was also happening at the time when you had all those histrionic and I stress histrionic headlines about the US getting ready to invade Greenland and Europe pretending it was going to send armed forces there, which of course we again discussed in the first segment here.
turns.zh: 所以这并不完全令人意外。而且那也是在所有那些歇斯底里的——我强调是歇斯底里的——标题出现的时候，说美国准备入侵格陵兰，欧洲假装要派军队去那里。这些我们在第一部分也讨论过。

turns.en: But it's not a complete surprise it's happened. What I think is important to me in that is, A, is being revealed because you didn't have to reveal that, but B, when you have the regular discussion about what Canada is or isn't doing with this elbows up, you know, campaign, which is very popular under Mark Carney within Canada and I get why I'm not trying to make any value judgment or be normative.
turns.zh: 但这并不完全令人意外。我认为对我来说重要的是，第一，这件事被公开了——因为你不必公开它。第二，当你定期讨论加拿大在这种「强硬起来」（elbows up）运动中做什么或不做什么时——这在 Mark Carney 领导下在加拿大国内非常受欢迎，我理解为什么——我不是要做任何价值判断或规范性评价。

turns.en: You obviously have an economic trade-off saying, well, we are incredibly deeply integrated with the US in a way which many people fail to understand, but we're going to try and distance ourselves from the US and try and basically join the European Union or come as close to doing that as possible.
turns.zh: 你显然面临一个经济取舍：我们与美国的整合程度极深——这是很多人无法理解的——但我们要试图与美国保持距离，基本上试图加入欧盟（European Union）或尽可能接近加入。

turns.en: If you look at just the economic side of that argument, it doesn't make any sense to anyone except the most starry-eyed Canadian and European optimist because Canada produces high-end value-added industrial goods in the few key sectors which are completely integrated with the US and are often sold to the US and it produces raw materials.
turns.zh: 如果你只看这个论证的经济面，除了最幻想的加拿大和欧洲乐观主义者之外，这对任何人来说都说不通。因为加拿大生产的是高端附加值的工业产品——在几个完全与美国整合的关键领域——通常销往美国；以及原材料。

turns.en: That's what it's tradeable goods are. Now, Europe would like to get its hand on the raw materials. Europe can buy those raw materials from Canada right now.
turns.zh: 这就是加拿大可贸易商品的全部。现在，欧洲想得到那些原材料，但欧洲现在就可以从加拿大购买那些原材料。

turns.en: There's no need to have any kind of new trading relationship to deal with those. Europe does not want to buy Canadian cars. Europe does not want to buy Canadian trains.
turns.zh: 不需要建立任何新的贸易关系来处理这些。欧洲不想买加拿大的汽车，欧洲不想买加拿大的火车。

turns.en: Europe does not want to buy Canadian jets. It has enough of its own. So Canada would be facing an economic future in which it disentangles itself with an economy which is just about two hours drive for most of Canadians going south when 90% of its population lives to trade more with a block on the other side of the Atlantic, which doesn't want to buy its high-evaluated goods and only wants to buy its raw materials.
turns.zh: 欧洲不想买加拿大的飞机，它自己有足够的。所以加拿大将面临一个经济未来——与一个大多数加拿大人只需向南开两小时车就能到达的经济体脱钩——而90%的加拿大人口就住在那条线附近——转而与大西洋彼岸的一个集团做更多贸易，而那个集团不想买它的高附加值产品，只想买它的原材料。

turns.en: Great. I don't think that's much of a sensible strategy, no matter how much one dislikes what Trump is doing and saying, but you can model that as an economist and it's not pretty what comes up.
turns.zh: 太好了。我不认为这是一个明智的战略，无论你多么不喜欢 Trump 的所作所为和言论。但作为一个经济学家你可以建模，结果并不好看。

turns.en: What Carney has just shown you is exactly what geo-strategists like myself and others, when we've been having conversations about this, let's walk away from the U.S., national strategy or grand strategy, have been saying, soto voce, which is this has staggeringly bad fat tail risks on the downside, and where's the upside?
turns.zh: Carney 刚刚展示的，正是像我这样的地缘战略家和其他人在讨论「离开美国」的国家战略或大战略时一直在低声说的——这有极其糟糕的下行尾部风险（fat tail risks），而上行空间在哪里？

turns.en: Because if you're saying, okay, maybe, maybe things can work out with Europe in the long run, maybe, maybe, and it's worth five, 10 years of pain to get there, but we know it's going to be very painful.
turns.zh: 因为如果你说，好吧，也许长期来看与欧洲的关系能行得通，也许吧，值得忍受五到十年的痛苦来达到那个目标。但我们知道那会非常痛苦。

turns.en: Again, I don't think the maths there, but let's say that's possible. If you then say it's a national strategy, we move from having complete peace and security on our southern border, like absolute complete peace and security, and of course, we've got problems potentially with Russia and the Arctic maybe in the future, and again, how are we going to fight Russia when you've got no real military, and of course, China might start
turns.zh: 再说一次，我不认为数学上说得通，但就算假设那是可能的。如果你再说这是一项国家战略——我们从南部边境拥有完全的和平与安全——绝对的和平与安全——转变过来。当然我们未来可能与俄罗斯在北极有问题，而且——你根本没有真正的军队，怎么跟俄罗斯打？当然中国可能在未来某个时候

turns.en: coming through that space with Russia at some point in the future, and again, that's going to cost a lot of money to confront. It will cost a lot more to do it without the Americans, but if they then say, well, maybe we've got the Americans as an actual enemy south of our border, and or they might invade, and I stress the Canadian army, when they did that exercise, came to the conclusion the best response was to run to the hills and fight like the Afghanistan Mujahideen, as in running
turns.zh: 开始与俄罗斯一起穿过那片空间，这又要花很多钱来应对。没有美国人的话成本会高得多。但如果他们接着说，好吧，也许我们南边的美国人实际上是敌人，而且他们可能入侵——我强调一下，加拿大军队在做那个推演时得出的结论是，最佳应对是跑到山里像阿富汗圣战者（Mujahideen）那样战斗——就是跑进

turns.en: into town and shooting things and then running back up to the hills again. Is that really an upside-downside, here's where we could be in the best of scenarios, here we could be in the worst of scenarios.
turns.zh: 城镇射击然后跑回山里。这真的是一个上行-下行分析吗？最好的情景下我们可能在这里，最坏的情景下我们可能在那里。

turns.en: Does that make any real geostrategic sense? I've been saying the same thing over and over again, and it's very unpopular in some circles, and it's not trying to be normative, and it's not trying to offend anybody, but it seems to me really bizarre in the same way that if Brexit for the UK had had the downside that maybe we end up with a war with Europe, I think the rationale for having done it one
turns.zh: 这在真正的地缘战略上有意义吗？我一直在反复说同样的事情，这在某些圈子里非常不受欢迎。我不是要做规范性评价，也不是要冒犯任何人。但在我看来这真的很奇怪——就像如果英国脱欧（Brexit）的下行风险可能是与欧洲开战，我认为做这个决定的理由

turns.en: way or the other would shift dramatically from just the economic argument, but that's potentially, given that Karny's carried out this exercise, what in the long run could be on the cards, because in the same way that the US is going to insist Canada has to have the same external tariff as it versus China, and that's what this is about really, and why maybe we'll come to that in a moment.
turns.zh: 将会从纯粹的经济论证发生巨大转变。但鉴于 Carney 已经做了这个推演，从长远来看这可能是摆在桌面上的选项。因为正如美国将坚持加拿大必须对中国的对外关税与美国一致——这才是这件事的核心——也许我们一会儿再谈这个。

turns.en: Do you really think the US is going to accept a Canada which drifts away from it geopolitically, starts doing deals with China, maybe, or with Europe, and then who knows where Europe goes in the future, and have a long, open, undefended border with it?
turns.zh: 你真的认为美国会接受一个在地缘政治上逐渐疏远它、开始与中国或欧洲做交易——而且谁知道欧洲未来会走向何方——并与之共享漫长、开放、无防御边境的加拿大吗？

turns.en: That doesn't make any sense geostrategically, and so the games that are being played here are for the very, very high stakes possible, but I think there's a lot more to be lost than one.
turns.zh: 这在地缘战略上说不通。所以这里正在进行的博弈赌注非常非常高，但我认为可能失去的远多于得到的。

turns.en: Well, and you were a geostrategist, I'm just a simpleton. I would just dumb that down further to, I know, lots and lots of American civilians and lots and lots of Canadian civilians, and none of them hate each other.
turns.zh: 嗯，你是地缘战略家，我只是个简单人。我只需把这个进一步简化为：我认识很多很多美国平民和很多很多加拿大平民，他们彼此之间没有任何仇恨。

turns.en: They're all fine. It's only the governments that seem to think that we should be at odds with each other, and it's amazing to me that this is happening in my lifetime growing up.
turns.zh: 他们都相处得很好。只有政府似乎认为我们应该彼此对立。让我惊讶的是，这竟然发生在我有生之年——在我成长的过程中，

turns.en: I really didn't expect it. We should probably move on now, 15 minutes in, and we haven't even got to the beginning of what we said we would cover today, which is all of these things that are happening, and I'll call it the eastern half of the world, whether it be the South China Sea, the incidents that have happened, North Korea testing hypersonic weapons, a lot of speculation that Xi Jinping has designs on invading Taiwan for the purpose of repatriating Taiwan as part of China, which
turns.zh: 我真的没有预料到这一点。我们现在应该继续了——已经过了15分钟，我们甚至还没有触及我们说过今天要讨论的内容的开头。也就是所有这些正在发生的事情——我把它称为世界的东半球——无论是南海、已经发生的事件、朝鲜测试高超音速武器、大量猜测习近平有意入侵台湾以将台湾回归为中国的一部分——

turns.en: of course China has said that they think Taiwan has always been part of China. The Taiwanese have a different opinion on that one. It seems to me these things are all important topics, but if I step back from it, I think the modern day equivalent of the Soviet U.S. Cold War is the U.S. China Cold War, and just like Vietnam, if you were smart enough to understand it, all played into a much bigger picture, I think all these things play into U.S. China Cold War somehow.
turns.zh: 当然中国已经表示他们认为台湾一直是中国的一部分。台湾人对此有不同的看法。在我看来这些都是重要的话题，但如果我退后一步来看，我认为现代版的苏联-美国冷战就是美中冷战。就像越南一样——如果你足够聪明能理解的话——它都是一个更大图景的一部分。我认为所有这些事情都以某种方式与美中冷战有关。

turns.en: I just am not smart enough to figure it out. Am I on the right track? You are bang on the right track. That's exactly what almost everything is about in one way or another, and having grasped that, you know, you're already halfway to the answers, and then one just has to join dots between different things.
turns.zh: 只是我还不够聪明把它搞清楚。我的方向对吗？你完全走对了方向。几乎所有事情都与此有关，以这样或那样的方式。一旦抓住了这一点，你知道，你已经走完了通往答案的一半路程。然后只需要把不同的点连起来。

turns.en: So let me just do a little bit of that dot joining for you. So it leads back to everything, including Russia, Ukraine, including the war we have in the Middle East, because it's not just the U.S. versus China.
turns.zh: 所以让我为你做一点连点工作。这一切都追溯到所有事情——包括俄罗斯、乌克兰，包括我们在中东的战争——因为这不只是美国对中国。

turns.en: It's not. It's the U.S. with a constellation of countries around it, who are themselves involved in various different open and closed negotiations with the U.S. over where they will sit within that block or whether they want to sit within it at all.
turns.zh: 不是。是美国加上围绕它的一群国家——这些国家自身也在与美国进行各种公开和封闭的谈判，讨论它们将在那个集团中处于什么位置，或者它们是否想要待在里面。

turns.en: So literally the Canadian example I just gave you, obviously the U.S. needs Canada by its side, but it needs a Canada that's reindustrialized, remilitarized, spending a lot more on defense and prepared to actually join it in terms of whatever adventures the U.S. is going to get involved in and will necessarily have to get involved in.
turns.zh: 所以我刚才给你的加拿大例子——显然美国需要加拿大站在它身边，但它需要一个再工业化、再军事化、在国防上花费更多、并准备真正加入美国将要参与的任何冒险行动的加拿大。

turns.en: That cannot be a Canada which runs its own independent trade policy because it might say, great, we want to do a deal with China when the U.S. doesn't, well then you can't do a deal with the U.S.
turns.zh: 这不能是一个奉行独立贸易政策的加拿大。因为它可能会说，太好了，我们想在美国不想的时候跟中国做交易——那你就不能跟美国做交易了。

turns.en: It's as simple as that. The logic has been crystal clear for years to me, and I've expressly put that in print. So that's part of it. But then that of course means Canada loses sovereignty because effectively it's within an EU-style structure within North America where the U.S. gets to set the external tariff and then everyone benefits underneath that umbrella and it's underneath the U.S. security
turns.zh: 就是这么简单。多年来这个逻辑对我来说一直非常清晰，我也已经明确把它写下来了。所以这是其中一部分。但这当然意味着加拿大失去了主权，因为它实际上处于一个北美版的欧盟式结构中，美国设定对外关税，然后所有人在那个保护伞下受益，而且是在美国的安全

turns.en: directive, which it kind of is within NATO anyway. So that's just one example. Europe also sits within that. Europe's flirting with Canada. There's a lot of tension between Europe and the U.S. as there was over Greenland.
turns.zh: 指导下——在 NATO 框架内其实已经是这样了。所以这只是一个例子。欧洲也处于那个结构中。欧洲在与加拿大调情。欧洲和美国之间有很多紧张关系，就像格陵兰问题上的紧张一样。

turns.en: And then of course we get that Greenland deal, which we spoke about in the first part, which by the way, removes sovereignty from Denmark, as I said, and Canada reproves of.
turns.zh: 然后当然我们有了那个格陵兰协议——我们在第一部分谈过——顺便说一下，它剥夺了丹麦的主权，正如我所说的，而加拿大对此表示赞同。

turns.en: So Canada, this country that's saying it has to keep its sovereignty, doesn't have a problem with Denmark losing military sovereignty over Greenland, which belongs to Denmark, provided that there's now security in North America.
turns.zh: 所以加拿大——这个说自己必须保持主权的国家——对丹麦失去对格陵兰的军事主权没有问题（格陵兰属于丹麦），只要北美现在有了安全保障。

turns.en: So all the Western allies are themselves jostling to get into the U.S. camp. But on the other camp, it's not just China. China has made abundantly clear that it works very, very closely with Russia and Russia cannot lose the war with Ukraine.
turns.zh: 所以所有西方盟友自己都在争抢进入美国阵营。但在另一个阵营，不只是中国。中国已经非常明确地表示它与俄罗斯的合作非常非常紧密，而俄罗斯不能输掉与乌克兰的战争。

turns.en: That's an open statement from China in various different circles. And everyone can see that in terms of the support that it's providing to Russia in various different ways.
turns.zh: 这是中国在不同场合的公开声明。每个人都可以从它以各种不同方式向俄罗斯提供的支持中看出这一点。

turns.en: But it's not just the two of them. Iran has a very, very close relationship with Russia. The drones, which are currently striking Ukraine, are originally an Iranian design.
turns.zh: 但不只是他们两个。伊朗与俄罗斯有非常非常紧密的关系。目前正在打击乌克兰的无人机最初是伊朗的设计。

turns.en: The Russians have improved them and put your engines on them, and they're now much faster than Ukrainian drone interceptors. And Russia is really, really hitting Ukraine hard.
turns.zh: 俄罗斯人改进了它们并安装了他们的引擎，现在它们比乌克兰的无人机拦截器快得多。俄罗斯正在非常非常猛烈地打击乌克兰。

turns.en: And it's not seeing a response that Ukraine can match at the moment. Those drones with Russian engines may soon find their way back to Iran to be fired at the U.S., Israel, and other forces in the region.
turns.zh: 而且乌克兰目前看不到能够匹敌的回应。那些装有俄罗斯引擎的无人机可能很快会被送回伊朗，用来向美国、以色列和该地区的其他力量发射。

turns.en: So there's already deep collaboration going on there. Then we can bring in North Korea, which has had periods of frosty relations with some of those other powers, but at the moment is again being at least supported by them in the same way that you might have a really angry dog in the neighborhood that you throw red meat to so that it doesn't bite you.
turns.zh: 所以那里已经有深度的合作在进行。然后我们可以把朝鲜加进来——它与其中一些大国有过关系冰冻期，但目前又再次得到它们的支持——就像你邻居有一条非常凶的狗，你扔红肉给它让它不咬你一样。

turns.en: And we are seeing North Korea developing hypersonic missiles. We are seeing North Korea looking around and thinking how it can help the others.
turns.zh: 我们看到朝鲜正在发展高超音速导弹（hypersonic missiles）。我们看到朝鲜在环顾四周，思考它能如何帮助其他国家。

turns.en: And in particular, it's rumored that it will send 50,000 men on top of any others that it may have already sent to fight against Ukraine with Russia and lots of munitions, which is also selling to Russia.
turns.zh: 特别是，有传闻说它将在已经可能派出的人员之外再派50,000人去与俄罗斯一起对抗乌克兰，以及大量弹药——它也在向俄罗斯出售弹药。

turns.en: So it's not just one country, the U.S., against one country, China. It's a constellation with rough and smooth edges and variable margins, if you will, on both sides.
turns.zh: 所以这不是一个国家（美国）对抗一个国家（中国）。而是双方各有一个由粗糙和光滑边缘组成的星座，margins 各不相同——如果你愿意这么说的话。

turns.en: And so when you look at North Korea firing hypersonic missiles, they are attempting to put pressure on South Korea alongside China, which is saying, well, at South Korea, we have a great economic relationship.
turns.zh: 所以当你看到朝鲜发射高超音速导弹时，它们正在试图与中国一起对韩国施压。中国在说，嘿韩国，我们有很好的经济关系。

turns.en: Do you really want to ruin that by being with the U.S.? And every country is being pushed and pulled between the two different blocks. On the other hand, by the way, just very quickly, I'll shut up for a second, we've just seen in the last 24 hours too, almost every country bar a few in Central and South America join a Dunro doctrine declaration saying that they all want to basically move towards economic
turns.zh: 你真的想因为跟美国在一起而毁掉这种关系吗？每个国家都在两个不同的集团之间被推来拉去。另一方面，顺便说一下——很快说完我就闭嘴——在过去24小时里，我们也看到除了中南美洲少数几个国家之外的几乎所有国家都加入了一项 Donroe 主义宣言，表示它们都要共同走向经济

turns.en: security together and fight narco terrorism together. And I would imagine in brackets, fight Chinese, Russian, and Iranian influence together.
turns.zh: 安全并共同打击毒品恐怖主义（narco terrorism）。我想象在括号里是——共同对抗中国、俄罗斯和伊朗的影响力。

turns.en: So the U.S. really is doing a grand job of rallying the troops, Canada aside, Nicaragua aside, Brazilian election aside, in the Western Hemisphere, and in Asia, it's much more contested territory.
turns.zh: 所以美国在西半球确实做得非常出色——在团结盟友方面——加拿大除外、尼加拉瓜除外、巴西大选除外。而在亚洲，这是更加有争议的领地。

turns.en: So everyone in the region is being squeezed in different ways. The South China Sea is a potential flashpoint too. And there, the Philippines is working very, very closely with Japan and with the U.S.
turns.zh: 所以该地区的每个人都在以不同方式被挤压。南海也是一个潜在的爆发点。在那里，菲律宾正在与日本和美国非常非常紧密地合作。

turns.en: And of course, the U.S. has a mutual defense treaty with the Philippines, but you are seeing China gradually try and squeeze Philippine possessions in the South China Sea, mainly through Coast Guard vessels, you know, ramming up against each other.
turns.zh: 当然，美国与菲律宾有共同防御条约（mutual defense treaty），但你看到中国在逐渐试图挤压菲律宾在南海的据点——主要通过海警船互相冲撞。

turns.en: And there, Taiwan has just sent a Coast Guard vessel to the Philippines, so you can see which side they take. Now, were we to get a flashpoint there, the U.S. would have a choice.
turns.zh: 在那里，台湾刚刚向菲律宾派遣了一艘海警船，所以你可以看到他们站在哪一边。现在，如果我们在那里遇到一个爆发点，美国将面临一个选择。

turns.en: Do we stand by a treaty ally and have to move forces against China in the South China Sea? Or do we, Salami style, say, okay, well, we'll let that ride?
turns.zh: 我们是支持条约盟友并必须在南海对中国动用武力？还是我们像切萨拉米香肠（salami slicing）一样说，好吧，我们就让这个过去？

turns.en: Which point? We understand completely that that defense guarantee doesn't stand out very much. You can Salami slice away in exactly the same way the Russians are talking about doing, you know, against Eastern Europe.
turns.zh: 到那个时候我们就完全理解了，那个防御保证并不那么靠得住。你可以用与俄罗斯人讨论对东欧做的一模一样的方式一片一片地切。

turns.en: We've just had today also, by the way, a Russian suicide drone has crashed in Romania. Not near Romania. In Romania. If anyone was killed, technically, that's a NATO Article 5 violation.
turns.zh: 顺便说一下，今天我们还有一件事——一架俄罗斯自杀式无人机坠毁在罗马尼亚。不是罗马尼亚附近，是在罗马尼亚境内。如果有人丧生，从技术上讲这就违反了 NATO 第五条（Article 5）。

turns.en: Russia has, you know, used military force against a NATO member. Are NATO immediately going to attack Russia? No, they're not. So we're already seeing this chipping away.
turns.zh: 俄罗斯对一个 NATO 成员国使用了军事力量。NATO 会立即攻击俄罗斯吗？不会。所以我们已经在看到这种蚕食。

turns.en: So that's happening, but I think a far larger argument, which you alluded to, which is really important, is this. There are serious discussions taking place in national security circles, and you can see some of them from time to time in the national media, and they appear briefly, then they disappear.
turns.zh: 所以这些正在发生。但我认为一个更大的论点——你也提到了——非常重要。在国家安全圈子里正在进行严肃的讨论，你偶尔能在主流媒体上看到一些，它们短暂出现然后消失。

turns.en: The Xi Jinping is deadly serious about past statements he's made, and that he would consider moving on Taiwan next year. Now, the concept of China moving on Taiwan is something that's not new.
turns.zh: 习近平对他过去的表态是非常认真的，他会考虑在明年对台湾采取行动。中国对台湾采取行动这个概念并不是什么新鲜事。

turns.en: You brought it up, and it's hardly a topic that is, you know, so left field that no one could imagine it. No one knows if that's true or not.
turns.zh: 是你提出来的，这也不是一个左得到没人能想象的话题。没有人知道那是不是真的。

turns.en: And what we can say is, if it were to happen, no one knows what the outcome would be, but the worst case scenario would be that you then have the US and China involved in a shooting match in Asia, on top of the fact that Ukraine and Russia would still be on one, and you'd still have the Middle East in flames.
turns.zh: 我们可以说的是，如果它真的发生了，没有人知道结果会怎样。但最坏的情景是——你将看到美国和中国在亚洲卷入一场枪战，再加上乌克兰和俄罗斯仍在交战，中东仍在燃烧。

turns.en: And that's really starting to look like at least a small scale world war in the worst case scenario. But here's where it links back to some of the other things that we're seeing.
turns.zh: 在最坏的情景下，这真的开始看起来像是一场至少小规模的世界大战。但这里是它与我们正在看到的其他事情的联系。

turns.en: If you suspect that's going to happen, and you're the US, and this is where you have to hypothesize after having structurally put forward the framework that they already have that there is a reason why these things are happening.
turns.zh: 如果你怀疑那将会发生，而且你是美国——这就是你必须在已经结构性地提出了框架之后进行假设的地方——这些事情发生是有原因的。

turns.en: If you're the US and you think, you know what, this is not beyond the realms of possibility, we can see the risk that could happen. Maybe it's 70-30, maybe it's 50-50, maybe it's 30-70 the other way.
turns.zh: 如果你是美国，你觉得，你知道吗，这并非不可能，我们可以看到那种风险。也许是70-30，也许是50-50，也许是30-70反过来。

turns.en: We don't want to run that risk because the war against Iran has already exposed that we actually don't have enough interceptors, we don't have enough bunker fuel in Hawaii anymore for the Pacific Fleet, there are lots and lots of areas that we're short of what we would need to fight that sustained war on the other side of the Pacific, and China is going to have home advantage.
turns.zh: 我们不想冒那个风险，因为对伊朗的战争已经暴露出我们实际上没有足够的拦截弹（interceptors），我们在夏威夷不再有足够太平洋舰队使用的船用燃料（bunker fuel），有很多很多领域我们缺乏在太平洋另一边打一场持久战所需的东西，而中国将拥有主场优势。

turns.en: What can we do between now and then to try very hard to persuade China not to do that? And you've got two options, haven't you, if you think logically.
turns.zh: 从现在到那时，我们能做什么来非常努力地说服中国不要那样做？如果你逻辑地思考，你有两个选择。

turns.en: One of them is you do some kind of deal. Now we have a Trump-Xi summit taking place at the moment, and all kinds of things are on the table and being discussed there.
turns.zh: 其中之一是达成某种协议。现在我们有一场 Trump-习峰会正在进行，各种事情都在桌面上被讨论。

turns.en: No one knows exactly what, but it has very much a Tehran, Potsdam, Yalta, and a World War II feel to it, to an extent. Let's wait and see the news headlines that come out.
turns.zh: 没有人确切知道是什么，但它非常有德黑兰（Tehran）、波茨坦（Potsdam）、雅尔塔（Yalta）和二战的感觉——在某种程度上。让我们拭目以待看会有什么新闻标题出来。

turns.en: But if you don't do a deal, then the only other option is you have to make that unviable in terms of being a strategic option for China to consider.
turns.zh: 但如果你不达成协议，那唯一的其他选择就是让这成为一个不可行的战略选项——让中国不再考虑它。

turns.en: Now, how do you do that? One on one end of the spectrum, you can say, well, okay, these are nuclear weapons and this is what they do. Do you want to think about that?
turns.zh: 那你怎么做到这一点？在光谱的一端，你可以说，好吧，这些是核武器，这是它们能做的事。你想考虑一下吗？

turns.en: Because that immediately takes us to the 10 seconds to midnight scenario, where if the other side says, okay, well, I think you're going to blink, we really are an incredibly dangerous world, and I don't want to even think about that, but I'm putting it forward as a logical possibility.
turns.zh: 因为那立即把我们带到「午夜前十秒」（10 seconds to midnight）的情景——如果对方说，好吧，我认为你会先眨眼——我们真的处于一个极其危险的世界。我不想甚至去考虑那个，但我把它作为一个逻辑可能性提出来。

turns.en: But if you're not going to do that at the other end of the spectrum, how about if the Russia-Ukraine war continues to drain global energy resources and keep Russia very occupied, how about bringing peace to that particular war where that to happen as a U.S. strategy might be some kind of lever to try and bring Russia on side with the U.S. against China, to kind of do a reverse Nixon, which is, I think, very unlikely, but I think the White
turns.zh: 但如果你在光谱的另一端不打算那样做，那么——如果俄乌战争继续消耗全球能源资源并让俄罗斯非常忙——给那场特定战争带来和平怎么样？如果这作为美国战略发生，可能是某种杠杆，试图把俄罗斯拉到美国一边对抗中国——做一个反向的 Nixon 策略。我认为这非常不太可能，但我认为白

turns.en: House is still open to that suggestion. And how about if the Middle East is so destabilized in all kinds of ways that anybody contemplating sustained military action in Asia without having any oil, now, of course, you can have your reserves of oil, but you might not be getting any flows of oil.
turns.zh: 宫仍然对那个建议持开放态度。那么——如果中东以各种方式变得如此不稳定，以至于任何人在没有石油的情况下考虑在亚洲进行持续军事行动——当然你可以有石油储备，但你可能得不到任何石油流量。

turns.en: How about that as the backdrop, but then saying how confident are you that you can manage to make that work with markets in total chaos and oil prices through the roof?
turns.zh: 把这个作为背景怎么样？但然后说，你有多大信心能在市场完全混乱、油价冲上天花板的情况下让这一切运转？

turns.en: So that is the larger picture that I'm describing. And I'm just in a bit of a state of shock, you know, if I really step back from all of this, Michael, I see a picture that scares the hell out of me, which is, look, go way back to, you know, the idea of don't listen to what they say, just watch what they do and figure out their intentions from that.
turns.zh: 这就是我描述的更大图景。而我只是有点震惊。你知道吗，如果我真的从所有这些中退后一步，Michael，我看到一幅让我吓得要死的图景。就是——回到那个理念：不要听他们说什么，看他们做什么，从中推断他们的意图。

turns.en: And I look at, okay, we had to have this conflict with Ukraine and Russia, which, as Barack Obama said, Ukraine is a vital interest to Russia and will never be a vital interest to the United States.
turns.zh: 我看了看，好吧，我们不得不与乌克兰和俄罗斯发生这场冲突。正如 Barack Obama 所说，乌克兰对俄罗斯来说是核心利益（vital interest），对美国来说永远不会是核心利益。

turns.en: A lot of people, myself included, just could not understand why we had to do this. The so-called unprovoked invasion was one of the most provoked events in world history.
turns.zh: 很多人——包括我自己在内——就是无法理解为什么我们必须这样做。所谓的「无端入侵」是世界历史上最被挑衅的事件之一。

turns.en: It started in February, not of 2022, but in February of 2014. And the people doing the provoking were not Russian, they were American. They were Hillary Clinton.
turns.zh: 它始于2月——不是2022年的2月，而是2014年的2月。而那些进行挑衅的人不是俄罗斯人，他们是美国人。他们是 Hillary Clinton。

turns.en: They were Victoria Newland. They were Jake Sullivan and they were Joe Biden. And that's where this all started in 2014. It eventually escalated.
turns.zh: 他们是 Victoria Nuland。他们是 Jake Sullivan，他们是 Joe Biden。这就是一切在2014年开始的地方。它最终升级了。

turns.en: We had the CIA doing things, but we had to somehow give this assistance to Ukraine and we had to ship all of these weapons to Ukraine. Then for a separate set of reasons, supposedly we just had to come to Israel's assistance because supposedly Iran was just two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon, which is nonsense.
turns.zh: 我们有 CIA 在做事情，但我们必须以某种方式向乌克兰提供援助，我们必须向乌克兰运送所有这些武器。然后出于另一组原因，据称我们不得不援助以色列，因为据称伊朗距离拥有核武器只有两周——这是胡说八道。

turns.en: But they were, and so we had to do this. It seems to me, if you step back and apply the, what are they doing as opposed to what they're saying?
turns.zh: 但他们确实是那样说的，所以我们不得不这样做。在我看来，如果你退后一步，运用「看他们做什么而不是说什么」的方法——

turns.en: It seems like somebody's trying to disarm the United States of America by tricking them into using up all their weapons and resources and giving them to other people.
turns.zh: 看起来有人在试图解除美利坚合众国的武装——通过诱骗他们把所有武器和资源用完并交给其他人。

turns.en: Okay. I mean, that's a viewpoint. There's some logic to it. I agree with you about the background to the Russia-Ukraine being far murkier than it's presented because people like simple narratives, particularly in geopolitics, particularly when you want one side to win.
turns.zh: 好的。我是说，这是一个观点。其中有一些逻辑。我同意你说的俄乌背景远比呈现出来的要混浊得多，因为人们喜欢简单的叙事——特别是在地缘政治中，特别是当你想要一方获胜时。

turns.en: It is complex. It is muddy. No one has clean hands. Far from absolving Russia for what they're doing to be abundantly clear. Okay. Well, it didn't mean to absolve Russia from anything, but to say it was completely unprovoked and Prutin just woke up one morning and was in a mood to invade somebody and there was no explanation.
turns.zh: 它是复杂的。它是混浊的。没有人是清白的。我绝不是在为俄罗斯的所作所为开脱——要说清楚。好的。嗯，这并不是要为俄罗斯开脱什么，而是要说它完全是无端挑衅的、Putin 某天早上醒来心情不好就想入侵某人、没有任何解释——

turns.en: There was no encroachment of NATO. There were no broken promises from the West. That's not telling the whole story. No. It's a more nuanced story at the very least, and within the Middle East, well, look, I can't think of a region that's more volatile than the Middle East, and the specifics of that, as we've discussed before, was that you don't want Iran to get a nuclear weapon.
turns.zh: 没有 NATO 的东扩，没有西方违背的承诺——这不是在讲完整的故事。不。这至少是一个更加微妙的故事。在中东方面，嗯，看，我想不出一个比中东更加动荡的地区。而具体情况——正如我们之前讨论过的——是你不想让伊朗获得核武器。

turns.en: Now, whether that was or wasn't true, none of us will ever know. But if that was even a 10% chance of that happening and the Middle East with all of its oil reserves then moving out of the US camp into another, that's not a chance you can take.
turns.zh: 现在，不管那是不是真的，我们永远不会知道。但如果那哪怕有10%的可能性发生，而中东——带着它所有的石油储备——从美国阵营转入另一个阵营，那不是你能承受的风险。

turns.en: Now, you can, as I said, then put those together and make the argument that you are, that somebody wants to try and disarm the US and have it use up all its forces ahead of time.
turns.zh: 现在你可以——正如我说的——把这些放在一起，构建这样一个论点：有人想要试图解除美国的武装，让它提前耗尽所有力量。

turns.en: That's up to people to listen to and to accept or not. My viewpoint is somewhat different, which is the US already had far fewer resources than it liked to think it did.
turns.zh: 这取决于人们自己去听、去接受或不接受。我的观点有些不同，那就是美国已经拥有了比它自以为的少得多的资源。

turns.en: It didn't realize how out of shape it was. This is painfully realistic for me. A guy in his mid-50s suddenly waking up and realizing, you know what, I'm not 30 anymore even though mentally you still think you are and actually trying to get fit and realizing my God, this hurts, and I can't keep up with everybody when mentally, because you look reasonably good in the mirror, you hadn't realized how far you'd slipped.
turns.zh: 它没有意识到自己的状态有多差。这对我来说是一个非常痛苦的现实比喻——一个五十多岁的男人突然醒来意识到，你知道吗，我不再是30岁了——尽管精神上你仍然觉得自己是——然后真的试图恢复健康，才发现天哪，这好痛，我跟不上所有人了。而精神上，因为你在镜子里看起来还不错，你没有意识到自己已经下滑了多远。

turns.en: That's pretty much where the US is, and against that backdrop, could the US take on a China with an industrial complex as strong as it is that can build a new ship in five minutes rather than five years, et cetera, et cetera, and if not, how do you then slow that down?
turns.zh: 美国基本上就处于这种状态。在那个背景下，美国能否对抗一个拥有如此强大工业复合体的中国——它能在五分钟而不是五年内造出一艘新船——等等等等？如果不能，你怎么减缓那个进程？

turns.en: Now, on one level, as we've already discussed in the past, you've flipped Venezuela effortlessly, relatively. Venezuela's oil is mine. That's not always going to work out well, but if you can at least make sure that other regions which provide key inputs into the Chinese industrial machine are destabilized whilst ring fencing everything you have at home from Canada all the way down to Argentina, which again, with one or two U-turns left to go, is on the cards, and one key election
turns.zh: 在一个层面上——正如我们过去已经讨论过的——你相对轻松地翻转了委内瑞拉。委内瑞拉的石油是我的了。这并不总是能顺利运作，但如果你至少能确保为中国特色工业机器提供关键投入的其他地区变得不稳定，同时把你国内的一切——从加拿大一直到阿根廷——都围起来保护好。这又还有一两个 U-turn 要走，还有一场关键选举

turns.en: left to go as well, that puts you in a far stronger position to then sit down and talk with China, because to give one more example of that, you've just seen just before the Trump Xi summit, that whereas last time China was coercing the US with rare earths, which it has total domination over the refining of, and the US agreed to this trade truce where tariffs on China are actually lower than they were before, and they're not being punished
turns.zh: 要过。这让你处于一个更强的位置来与中国坐下来谈判。再举一个例子——你刚刚看到就在 Trump-习峰会之前，上次中国用稀土（rare earths）来胁迫美国——它在稀土精炼方面拥有完全的统治地位——而美国同意了那个贸易休战，对中国的关税实际上比以前更低了。他们没有像人们预期的那样被美国

turns.en: by the US in quite the same way one would expect, and indeed other countries are also being hit too, so it doesn't look quite as narrowly against China as it might otherwise be seen as.
turns.zh: 严厉惩罚，而且确实其他国家也在被打击，所以看起来不像是那么狭义地针对中国。

turns.en: They agreed that trade truce last time, the last summit, and this time China asked to have that trade truce extended all the way through to the end of Trump's term, and Trump turned around and said, no, we only want to do it until early January.
turns.zh: 他们上次峰会同意了那个贸易休战。这次中国要求把贸易休战延长到 Trump 任期结束，而 Trump 转身说不，我们只想到一月初。

turns.en: So why are they not extending it? What do they know about what's going to happen over the next few months that tells them they don't have to have a trade truce with China, or they're prepared to at least signal to China that maybe they have a card to play, whereby China won't have quite the same whip and hand over them.
turns.zh: 那他们为什么不延长呢？他们对未来几个月将要发生的事情知道些什么，告诉他们不需要与中国保持贸易休战？或者他们准备至少向中国发出信号——也许他们有一张牌可以打，让中国不再对他们拥有同样的鞭子和控制力？

turns.en: Is there something happening with AI and mineral processing and some new miracle technology? I don't know. It's well outside my wheelhouse, but AI certainly seems to be doing many remarkable things above and beyond making very convincing videos of people doing silly things.
turns.zh: 在 AI 和矿物加工方面是否有什么新的奇迹技术在发生？我不知道。这远远超出了我的专业范围，但 AI 确实似乎在做很多了不起的事情——远不止制作非常逼真的人做蠢事的视频。

turns.en: So all kinds of things are shifting and changing. All kinds of stories can be misleading or hidden away on page 17, a bit of relevance to varying degrees, and yet the underlying dynamic is the US plus or minus others versus China plus or minus others.
turns.zh: 所以各种事情都在转变和变化。各种故事可能具有误导性，或者被藏在第17版，与不同程度的相关性。但底层的动态是美国加上或减去其他国家对抗中国加上或减去其他国家。

turns.en: And who's in the relatively stronger position to do what if both sides are afraid that they might be marching towards some kind of clash, and how you work to either prevent that or put yourself in the best position to benefit from it if it were to happen?
turns.zh: 如果双方都害怕自己可能正在走向某种冲突，那么谁处于相对更强的位置来做什么？你如何努力防止那种冲突，或者如果它真的发生了，如何让自己处于最佳位置从中获益？

turns.en: Michael, the economist just had a editorial about AI and how it has essentially become the new Cold War with China, and they said, if Trump really wants to have his Nobel Prize, what he ought to do is figure out how to have salt talks.
turns.zh: Michael，The Economist 刚刚发了一篇关于 AI 的社论，说它基本上已经变成了与中国的新型冷战。他们说如果 Trump 真的想拿到他的 Nobel Prize，他应该做的是想办法进行类似 SALT 的谈判。

turns.en: And for listeners who are not old enough to remember that, the Strategic Arms Limitation Treaties, way back, I don't remember if that was 70s or 80s, but a very long time ago when I was a lot younger than I am now, that was just all the news was US and Russia talking about limiting the number of nuclear warheads.
turns.zh: 对于那些太年轻不记得的听众来说——战略武器限制条约（Strategic Arms Limitation Treaties），很久以前——我不记得是70年代还是80年代——但很久以前我比现在年轻得多的时候，所有新闻都是关于美国和俄罗斯讨论限制核弹头数量。

turns.en: And what's being suggested now is Trump needs to have a big negotiation with Xi Jinping about how to stop an AI arms race, where we literally get into using AI for military advantage and it has the same effect as trying to amass the largest number of nuclear weapons.
turns.zh: 现在被建议的是 Trump 需要与习近平进行一场大谈判——关于如何阻止一场 AI 军备竞赛。在这场竞赛中我们真的会把 AI 用于军事优势，其效果与试图积累最大数量的核武器相同。

turns.en: We spend all of our resources trying to out AI each other. What if we could come to some kind of truce and cooperate rather than work against each other?
turns.zh: 我们把所有资源都花在试图在 AI 上压倒对方。如果我们能达成某种休战并合作而不是互相对抗呢？

turns.en: Does that make sense? Is that, is AI really going to be the next arms race? And if so, does it make sense to try to have a limitation talk about it?
turns.zh: 这有道理吗？AI 真的会是下一场军备竞赛吗？如果是的话，尝试进行限制谈判有意义吗？

turns.en: It does make sense. I believe that is happening. And again, there are different ways to look at that as a lens through which to then read all the other headlines that we see about it.
turns.zh: 这确实有道理。我相信这正在发生。同样，有不同的方式来审视这一点——作为一个视角来解读我们看到的所有其他相关标题。

turns.en: Because ostensibly, that argument has already been put forward by the US, but not by Trump. Trump has pushed back. Now that can be good cop, bad cop.
turns.zh: 因为表面上，这个论点已经由美国方面提出了——但不是由 Trump 提出的。Trump 进行了反驳。这可以是好警察坏警察（good cop, bad cop）的策略。

turns.en: It might be that he genuinely disagrees with other people around him. There have been many key players in the AI industry in the US saying, hey, yes, we want to see that happen.
turns.zh: 也可能是他真的与周围的其他人意见不同。美国 AI 行业有很多关键人物在说，嘿，是的，我们希望看到那发生。

turns.en: China's response initially to that was nobody tells us what to do, because they believe that while the US saying that they want to move to some kind of regulation, they're actually attempting to raise the drawbridge and say, we already have the Manhattan project moment.
turns.zh: 中国最初对此的回应是「没人能告诉我们该怎么做」——因为他们认为美国说想要走向某种监管，实际上是在试图拉起吊桥，说「我们已经有了曼哈顿工程（Manhattan Project）时刻。」

turns.en: We've already created AGI, artificial general intelligence, which is Skynet effectively, which will just get smarter and smarter. We already have it.
turns.zh: 我们已经创造了 AGI——通用人工智能（artificial general intelligence）——实际上就是 Skynet——它会越来越聪明。我们已经拥有了。

turns.en: You don't. So now we want regulation to make sure others can't get there. That's China's paranoia. They may or may not be right. And then I'm sure there are people infinitely closer to this, so it would have a far more granular view of it.
turns.zh: 你们没有。所以我们现在要监管，确保其他人也到不了那里。这是中国的偏执。他们可能是对的也可能不是。我确信有人比我更接近这个话题，会有更加细粒度的看法。

turns.en: But that appears to be one of the interpretations. Equally, it would be great if both parties could come together and say, yeah, we want to make sure that there's a level playing field, that neither of us will use it or weaponize it against each other.
turns.zh: 但这似乎是一种解读。同样，如果双方能走到一起说「是的，我们想确保有一个公平的竞争环境（level playing field），我们都不会用它来对付彼此或将其武器化」，那当然很好。

turns.en: I think that's desperately naive. Because in exactly the same way that we talk about that, and China is no fan of, for example, nuclear weapons, China is massively expanding its nuclear arsenal at the moment.
turns.zh: 我认为那是极度天真的。因为完全一样——我们谈论这个——而中国也不是核武器的粉丝——中国目前正在大规模扩充其核武库。

turns.en: So rather than saying to the US, we'll keep a small one. And let's talk about what else we can do to reduce yours and build bridges. They're throwing everything they've got at actually trying to build up their nuclear warhead counter to keep up with Russia and the US.
turns.zh: 所以与其对美国说「我们保持小规模，让我们谈谈还能做什么来减少你们的核武并建立桥梁」，他们正在倾尽全力来扩充核弹头数量以跟上俄罗斯和美国。

turns.en: So this isn't a backdrop, sadly, within which one can expect many of those kind of 1970s detente area policies to stick, but that doesn't mean people won't try, and that doesn't mean there aren't parties within the US that would like to see that, and there aren't parties within China that would like to see that, but that doesn't necessarily mean that they are the decision makers, because any polity, whether it's a red in tooth and claw democracy
turns.zh: 所以遗憾的是，这不是一个你可以期待很多那种1970年代缓和（detente）政策能奏效的背景。但这不意味着人们不会尝试，也不意味着美国内部没有希望看到这种情况的派系，中国内部也没有希望看到这种情况的派系。但这不一定意味着他们是决策者。因为任何政体——无论是像美国这样尖牙利爪的民主制度

turns.en: like the US, or whether it's the Chinese system, does still have different viewpoints and different parties, if not political parties, who think a different strategy might be preferable at different times.
turns.zh: 还是中国体制——确实都有不同的观点和不同的派系（如果不是政党的话），他们认为在不同时期不同的策略可能更可取。

turns.en: That doesn't mean that they're always the one actually setting the agenda. As you said, there are experts who know more than either of us about some of these topics.
turns.zh: 但这不意味着他们总是实际设定议程的人。正如你所说，有些专家比我们俩更了解这些话题中的某些方面。

turns.en: So I'd like to take a minute to summarize what Matt Berry told our audience a couple of weeks ago about a development that he predicts in AI that's very, very close to this issue in China.
turns.zh: 所以我想花一分钟总结一下 Matt Berry 几周前告诉我们听众的一个预测——关于 AI 领域的发展，与中国问题非常非常接近。

turns.en: What Matt is saying is, okay, everybody's focused on the frontier models, particularly anthropic and Claude is kind of the leader, and now, of course, open AI says the chat GPT-6 is better, they're neck and neck, and we're in the lead, and we are in the lead in the sense that those American AI frontier labs are producing the very best models, and guess what?
turns.zh: Matt 说的是，好吧，每个人都在关注前沿模型（frontier models）——特别是 Anthropic 和 Claude 算是领先者。现在当然 OpenAI 说 ChatGPT-6 更好，他们不相上下，我们在领先。而「我们在领先」的意思是那些美国 AI 前沿实验室正在生产最好的模型。猜猜怎么着？

turns.en: They're very expensive, and they're underwritten by a huge amount of investment, and it's not clear where the payback is. Meanwhile, in China, what's happening is open source AI models that you don't get the server, you can't just connect to it like go to Claude.ai and it works.
turns.zh: 它们非常昂贵，由大量投资支撑，而且不清楚回报在哪里。与此同时，在中国发生的是开源 AI 模型——你不能只是连接到一个服务器，不像去 Claude.ai 那样就能用。

turns.en: You have to actually buy your own hardware and install the thing and run it on your own hardware, but when you do, you get a massive advantage that Matt Berry thinks is going to completely upset the market.
turns.zh: 你必须实际购买自己的硬件并安装它，在你自己的硬件上运行。但当你这样做时，你获得了一个巨大的优势——Matt Berry 认为这将完全颠覆市场。

turns.en: And that advantage is you can air gap your enterprise from Anthropics Cloud so that they're not mining your proprietary information that you're getting Claude's help with in order to train their next model.
turns.zh: 那个优势就是你可以把你的企业与 Anthropic 的云端气隔（air gap），这样他们就不会挖掘你的专有信息——你在获取 Claude 帮助时分享的那些信息——来训练他们的下一个模型。

turns.en: And what Matt is saying is there could be a revolt where, yeah, these frontier labs in the US are making the best AI, but guess what? The open source models that you can get from China, if you're smart enough to now how to hook up your own hardware and do fancy stuff that's above my head, but Matt does it in his sleep, if you can do that stuff, what you end up with open source for free out of China is a model that's about as good as the frontier labs in the US were delivering three
turns.zh: Matt 说的是可能会有一场「反叛」——是的，美国的这些前沿实验室在做最好的 AI，但猜猜怎么着？如果你够聪明知道如何连接自己的硬件并做一些超出我理解范围的花哨操作——但 Matt 闭着眼都能做——如果你能做那些事情，你从中国的开源中免费得到的模型，其水平大约相当于美国前沿实验室三

turns.en: or four months ago. It's really catching up quickly. So Matt thinks we get to a point where people get sick of having their data mined and Anthropic is training on your, you know, the fine print says it's okay for them to keep all of your personal information that you shared with Claude in the middle of the night about your strategy for your business and they're going to train the next model on it.
turns.zh: 四个月前的交付水平。它追赶的速度真的很快。所以 Matt 认为我们会到达一个临界点——人们受够了自己的数据被挖掘。Anthropic 在训练你的——你知道的，细则里说他们可以保留你半夜与 Claude 分享的所有关于你商业战略的个人信息——他们要用来训练下一个模型。

turns.en: Matt thinks eventually that blows up and everybody says, I'd rather just get these Chinese models that are free and put them on my own hardware.
turns.zh: Matt 认为最终这会爆发，每个人都会说，我宁愿直接拿这些来自中国的免费模型放在自己的硬件上。

turns.en: What if that happens? What does that do to the US AI industry and what does Trump say about that one? I don't think he's going to respond too positively to that.
turns.zh: 如果那发生了怎么办？那会对美国 AI 产业造成什么影响？Trump 对此会怎么说？我不认为他会对此做出太积极的回应。

turns.en: Let's just consider this in its entirety. It's a clever argument and they're a far cleverer than people than me in the AI industry. But let's just be very cynical.
turns.zh: 让我们从整体来考虑这个问题。这是一个聪明的论点，而且 AI 行业里有比我聪明得多的人。但让我们非常愤世嫉俗地看一下。

turns.en: Take a step back and look at this within the context of, you know, what I call grand macro strategy, which is markets and grand strategy on a national perspective and national security perspective all together as the backdrop.
turns.zh: 退后一步，把这放在我所说的「大宏观战略」的语境中来看——即市场和大战略从国家视角和国家安全视角合在一起作为背景。

turns.en: Just run that past the smell test for a second, right? The argument is that China, as in state capitalism, we know what you're doing, CCTV cameras everywhere, Chinese EVs record everything.
turns.zh: 就把这个过一下「气味测试」（smell test）吧，好吗？论点是——中国，即国家资本主义——我们知道你在做什么。到处是 CCTV 摄像头，中国的电动汽车记录一切。

turns.en: The Norwegians reportedly recently put a Chinese EV bus in a quarry and found out that even when it wasn't plugged in with the engine on and nothing was running, it was trying to transmit data back to China.
turns.zh: 据报道挪威人最近把一辆中国电动公交车放在一个采石场里，发现即使没有插电、引擎开着、什么都没运行，它也在试图向中国传输数据。

turns.en: That China is happy developing an AI where you can air gap it and have your own proprietary little genius model doing its own thing without the state knowing what you're doing.
turns.zh: 而中国乐于开发一种你可以气隔的 AI——有你自己的专有小天才模型在那里做自己的事——而国家不知道你在做什么。

turns.en: But America, land of the brave home of the free, is going to be all about big brother leaning over your shoulder and watching what you're doing and telling you what to do.
turns.zh: 但美国——勇者之地、自由之家——却全是大哥哥（Big Brother）在你肩膀后面看着你做什么并告诉你该怎么做。

turns.en: Now I'm not ruling that out. I am saying it's highly unlikely given the prevailing political cultures and political economy in each country over the longer term.
turns.zh: 现在我不是在排除这种可能性。我是说，鉴于每个国家长期以来的主流政治文化和政治经济，这极不可能。

turns.en: What I would say therefore is I have seen suggestions, and again, if someone's got a better argument, feel free to, you know, just to immediately email or email Eric or dive in.
turns.zh: 因此我要说的是——我看到有这样的说法，同样如果有人有更好的论点，请随时发邮件给 Eric 或直接参与讨论。

turns.en: But actually a lot of the Chinese open source performance has been because they're effectively standing on the shoulders of the US models, that they're always three or four months behind because they're effectively just cloning them or just a shell, you know, where you effectively use one website to try and do something for you.
turns.zh: 但实际上很多中国开源的表现是因为它们实际上站在美国模型的肩膀上——它们总是落后三到四个月——因为它们实际上只是在克隆它们，或者只是一个外壳（shell）——你知道的——你实际上用一个网站来尝试为你做某事，

turns.en: And it just goes and asks the American AI to do it for it. Now, I don't know whether that's true. It may not be true for all of them, and I'm not an expert in the field.
turns.zh: 然后它只是去问美国 AI 来替它完成。现在，我不知道那是不是真的。对其中一些来说可能不是真的，我不是这个领域的专家。

turns.en: But if it is, I don't think that China doing that is anything other than attempt to try and undermine the model that American AI is working on, because they're afraid that actually it might keep moving so far ahead that it leaves them behind and seeing the AI industry crumble before America gets its hands on Skynet or whatever genius intelligence is going to need to run factories for it, to run the military for it, to do all kinds
turns.zh: 但如果确实如此，我不认为中国这样做是除了试图破坏美国 AI 正在努力的模型之外的任何事情。因为他们害怕它实际上可能继续遥遥领先，把他们甩在后面。看到 AI 产业在美国得到 Skynet 或任何天才智能之前崩溃——那种智能将需要运行工厂、运行军队、做各种

turns.en: of things in different dimensions, we can't imagine, to come up with technology to get around China's rare earth refining monopoly, et cetera, you name it, they want to blow that up using financial markets by just saying, well, you know, you're as a company, you don't make enough profit, you're going under before you get there.
turns.zh: 我们在不同维度无法想象的事情——开发出绕过中国稀土精炼垄断的技术等等——你能想到的都有。他们想利用金融市场来炸毁它——直接说，嗯，你知道的，作为一家公司你赚的利润不够，你还没到那一步就要倒闭了。

turns.en: That would be absolutely how Beijing runs its strategic book and how I would do it in their position too. But on the US side, just to finish off, I have argued repeatedly, you know, on podcasts and in print, that if you really genuinely think there is a Skynet at the end of this, this super intelligence within which you can then solve all problems, because it can basically create a super intelligence better than itself, which will come up with new ways to do all
turns.zh: 这绝对就是北京运营其战略账本的方式，也是我在他们的位置上会做的事。但在美国这边——最后说一下——我已经在播客和印刷品上反复论证过：如果你真的由衷地认为这最终会出现一个 Skynet——一个超级智能——在其中你可以解决所有问题，因为它基本上能创造出比自己更好的超级智能，想出在科学前沿做各种

turns.en: kinds of things at the edge of the scientific frontier. And I would say, you know, if you really want to get around all the kind of limits that we have, does it matter that the company blows up?
turns.zh: 事情的新方法。我会说，你知道吗，如果你真的想绕过我们所有的限制，那公司爆不爆掉有什么关系？

turns.en: I would actually argue it's a genius strategic move by the Americans to say, look, we can't afford X number of trillion dollars borrowing on top of the deficit we've already got to develop this technology, which is a one and done thing if we can.
turns.zh: 我实际上会论证这是美国人的一步天才战略棋：看，我们负担不起在已有赤字之上再借 X 万亿美元来开发这项技术——如果成功的话这是一锤子买卖。

turns.en: But we'd be very, very happy to have international capital, including Chinese capital, people all around the world buying shares in these companies, allowing them to do it.
turns.zh: 但我们非常非常乐意让国际资本——包括中国资本——全世界的人购买这些公司的股票，让它们来做这件事。

turns.en: And I would say it's national security and let the market do what it wants to do, which is bye bye and good night. That wouldn't surprise me.
turns.zh: 我会说这是为了国家安全，让市场做它想做的事——那就是 bye bye 和 good night。这一点也不会让我意外。

turns.en: It's not a forecast, but it's a real politic acceptance of the fact that if the US had had to outsource the Manhattan Project and nuclear weapons to private labs in Silicon Valley, because they couldn't afford to do it, they wouldn't have let them keep nuclear weapons at the end.
turns.zh: 这不是一个预测，而是一种现实政治（realpolitik）的接受——如果美国不得不把曼哈顿计划和核武器外包给硅谷的私人实验室（因为他们负担不起），他们最后不会让它们保留核武器。

turns.en: To be clear, I did not mean to suggest that China had altruistic intentions to deliver the world free AI because they just wanted to be nice guys.
turns.zh: 说清楚，我并不是要暗示中国有利他意图要给世界提供免费 AI——只因为他们想做好人。

turns.en: I think it's exactly what you said. I think that if you're China and you realize that you cannot realistically outcompete the frontier AI labs in the United States, which I do not think they could do, then what you do is say, let them spend all the money.
turns.zh: 我认为正如你说的。如果你是中国人，意识到你无法现实地在竞争中胜过美国的前沿 AI 实验室——我不认为他们能做到——那你就会说，让他们花所有的钱。

turns.en: And this is kind of what the Soviets did in the Cold War is they let the Americans spend more of the money and engineer all of the stuff. And in terms of designing their own spacecraft and so forth, there were documented cases where all they did was paid off in bribed Americans to leak plans of American designs and copied it.
turns.zh: 这有点像苏联人在冷战中所做的——他们让美国人花更多的钱、设计所有东西。在设计自己的航天器等方面，有记录显示他们所做的只是付钱贿赂美国人泄露美国设计的图纸然后照抄。

turns.en: I think that if you're China and you're running an economic war, you let the US spend all the money on the research. And as you said, you just try to copy their stuff and release it for free in a cycle that eventually does appeal.
turns.zh: 我认为如果你是中国并且你在打一场经济战，你就让美国花所有的钱在研发上。然后就像你说的，你只是试图复制他们的东西并免费发布——在一个最终会起作用的循环中。

turns.en: And yeah, I think it probably could be designed to send information back to China. But if anthropic stuff all runs in a cloud, and the stuff you can get in open source models from China can be run on air-gapped hardware of your own, it gives you more flexibility and it potentially could be China's intentional strategy to upset and crash the US AI boom.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为它可能被设计用来向中国回传信息。但如果 Anthropic 的东西都在云端运行，而你从中国获得的开源模型可以在你自己的气隔硬件上运行，那就给了你更多灵活性。这可能确实是中国故意的策略——来颠覆和摧毁美国的 AI 繁荣。

turns.en: Since Trump has after all said that his big thing is going to be leadership in AI and dominance in AI as a national strategy, if you're trying to attack that, what better way to undermine it than what Microsoft learned in the 90s, which is give stuff away for free to put your smaller competitors out of business.
turns.zh: 既然 Trump 毕竟说过他的大事业将是 AI 领域的领导地位和 AI 主导权作为国家战略——如果你想攻击那个目标，还有什么比 Microsoft 在90年代学到的教训更好的方式来削弱它呢——免费赠送东西来让你的小竞争对手倒闭。

turns.en: We're on the same page on that, but the important thing is to see it not just in the market terms, which matter to the investors who are listening, of course, but to understand the reasons why that might be happening, which is national security, on which I've got a couple of little related anecdotes I'm going to throw your way.
turns.zh: 我们在这一点上是一致的。但重要的是不仅要从市场角度来看——这对正在听的投资者当然重要——还要理解为什么会发生这种情况。那就是国家安全。关于这一点我有几个相关的小故事要抛给你。

turns.en: And they're all directly related to it, even if they kind of a little bit together. First of all, talking about technology, I remember a fantastic anecdote about the Soviet space program, where apparently a Soviet astronaut was up in space and he met one of the American, it was cosmonauts, they were called, and he met one of the American astronauts, I think on the International Space Station at some point, and the American astronaut
turns.zh: 它们都与此直接相关，即使它们看起来有点不搭。首先，说到技术——我记得一个关于苏联太空计划的绝妙故事。据说一名苏联宇航员在太空中遇到了一位美国宇航员——他们叫 cosmonauts——我想是在国际空间站（International Space Station）上的某个时候。那位美国宇航员

turns.en: was writing with that brilliant pen, which can write in zero gravity, which infamously was on that Seinfeld episode, if you remember, take the pen, one of my favorite episodes.
turns.zh: 正在用那种能在零重力下写字的神奇笔写字——这支笔臭名昭著地出现在那集 Seinfeld 里，如果你记得的话——「拿那支笔」——我最喜欢的集数之一。

turns.en: Anyway, so he was showing it off and explaining to the cosmonaut, well, our scientists spent ages getting the right nib and the ink flow that can work in zero gravity, etc, etc, etc. What do you use or how did you do it?
turns.zh: 总之，他在那里炫耀并向 cosmonaut 解释，嗯，我们的科学家花了很长时间才搞对了笔尖和墨水流量使其能在零重力下工作等等等等。你们用什么？你们是怎么做到的？

turns.en: And the Soviet cosmonaut said, we use pencil. Exactly. And which you call it, exactly. So that's one. The second one is this. I lived in Moscow when I was much younger, much younger, a different world, different time. And one of the areas of Moscow that I used to go and visit from time to time, because there was a good Georgian restaurant there, was called Zelenograd.
turns.zh: 苏联 cosmonaut 说，我们用铅笔。没错。你怎么叫它来着，没错。所以这是第一个。第二个是这样的。我年轻得多时住在莫斯科——年轻得多，一个不同的世界、不同的时代。我偶尔会去莫斯科的一个区域参观——因为那里有一家很好的格鲁吉亚餐厅——叫做 Zelenograd。

turns.en: Zelenograd at that point was a closed science city. So it had like internal passports above and beyond the internal passports you needed within the Soviet Union. And the people within it couldn't meet foreigners at all.
turns.zh: Zelenograd 当时是一个封闭的科学城。所以它有内部护照——在苏联境内已经需要的内部护照之上还有额外的。里面的人完全不能见外国人。

turns.en: And, you know, I think there were even restrictions on how many ordinary Soviet citizens they could meet, because what they were doing or what they were thinking was so important that they weren't allowed to just suddenly meet other people.
turns.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为甚至对他们能见多少普通苏联公民也有限制，因为他们所做的或所想的是如此重要，不允许他们随便见其他人。

turns.en: We still, as we were alluding to earlier with energy, when I'm saying we have a one world because markets energy system in a world in which we are attempting to get the upper hand over each other. And some countries have energy and some countries don't.
turns.zh: 就像我们刚才提到的能源问题——当我说我们有一个「因为市场」的一体化世界能源系统——在一个我们试图互相占据上风的世界里。有些国家有能源，有些没有。

turns.en: So why does it make sense to share it one world with everybody if you have it and they don't? If you have cutting edge technology, why the hell are you allowing people to fly wherever they want internationally? I'm not being normative.
turns.zh: 那为什么如果你有的话跟所有人共享一个世界是合理的——如果他们没有？如果你有尖端技术，你为什么要允许人们随意飞往国际任何地方？我不是在做规范性评价。

turns.en: I'm just thinking out loud, looking at past examples, projecting dots. That's my methodology. How long until people at Harvard or other leading universities where I can assure you from knowing people who work at top universities, you know, a huge sway of these academics are either so apolitical, they don't understand China, America.
turns.zh: 我只是在出声思考，看着过去的例子，投射连点。这是我的方法论。还要多久——在 Harvard 或其他顶尖大学的人们——我可以向你保证，从我认识在顶尖大学工作的人那里了解到——大量学者要么是完全不关心政治的，他们不理解中国、美国——

turns.en: What are these? These are just concepts. I don't mind. Or they're so naive. They don't realize when someone rocks up, you know, from from another country with a very suspicious CD, and they say, can I work with you on top secret project?
turns.zh: 这些是什么？这些只是概念。我不在意。——要么是如此天真，他们没有意识到当某人从另一个国家带着一个非常可疑的 U 盘出现并说「我能和你一起做这个绝密项目吗？」

turns.en: And you say, of course you can come and work with me on the bench and others openly, politically, quite anti-American or anti-Western, because that's very fashionable now in circles, as you know. And some of them, frankly, are not paid very much and can be bribed very easily.
turns.zh: 你会说，当然你可以来和我一起做。在实验台上，其他人则公开地在政治上相当反美或反西方——因为那在现在的圈子里非常时髦，你知道的。而且坦率地说他们中一些人报酬不高，很容易被收买。

turns.en: You put all that together and that's absolute liability. How our national security thinking hasn't realized that you can't have like, you know, because markets operating in science in the same way you can't have it operating in energy if you're in a zero-sum competition, which we are. Alludes me.
turns.zh: 把这些放在一起，那就是绝对的安全隐患。我们的国家安全思维怎么还没有意识到——在零和竞争中（我们确实处于零和竞争），你不能在科学领域实行「因为市场」的运作方式，就像你不能在能源领域那样做一样。这让我困惑。

turns.en: And then the final point on that is Chinese EVs. They're great. Okay. I'm not anti-Chinese EVs. How many can you buy in America? None. So if that model is already existing, which is this is a threat to us, we don't like it, it's better, can't have it. Why isn't that going to be extended to open source stuff from China too, imminently, and then potentially even to American universities, etc., etc.
turns.zh: 然后最后一点是关于中国电动汽车。它们很棒。好吧，我不反对中国电动汽车。你在美国能买到多少？一辆都买不到。所以如果那种模式已经存在了——就是「这对我们构成威胁，我们不喜欢它，它更好，不能拥有」——为什么这不会很快扩展到来自中国的开源产品？然后甚至可能扩展到美国大学等等。

turns.en: If you come in to work with us, you can't go home, etc. None of that would surprise me. But then, you know, some people are surprised we've got a potential 90-day diesel export ban being discussed. So that wasn't possible. And that's always been on the cards for me too for the same kind of reasons.
turns.zh: 如果你来和我们一起工作，你就不能回家了。等等。这些都不会让我意外。但然后，你知道，有些人对我们讨论一个可能的90天柴油出口禁令感到惊讶。所以那也不是不可能的。对我来说这一直在可能发生的范围内——出于同样的原因。

turns.en: As you were talking, I couldn't help but think more about the AI thing. If you see this as a long game and you really think that where we're headed is a U.S. versus China Cold War that eventually culminates in a major, you know, World War III kind of conflict.
turns.zh: 你说话的时候，我不禁更多地思考 AI 的事情。如果你把这看作一盘长棋，你真的认为我们的方向是一场美中冷战——最终以一场重大的、你知道的、第三次世界大战式的冲突收场。

turns.en: But by the way, I don't switch into it. I don't think that. I think they think that on some sites. And that's what, you know, some players are, some people may be in favor of that. Some people may be opposed in trying to do whatever they can to prevent it. I'm not saying I see that. I want to be abundantly clear. That's not my forecast. I'm recognizing that other people, you know, where epaulets might see that. Please carry on.
turns.zh: 但顺便说一下，我不赞同这个。我不那么认为。我认为他们中有些人那样想。这就是——你知道的——一些参与者，有些人可能赞成那样，有些人可能反对并试图尽一切力量阻止它。我不是说我看到那个。我要非常清楚地说明，那不是我的预测。我只是承认其他人——你知道的——肩章上有条纹的人可能那样看。请继续。

turns.en: Okay. Let's suppose that some people in China are thinking that way. What could possibly be a more clever strategy than to say, let's let the USAI labs do all the hard work, we'll copy their models, we'll open source them, we'll also have people that are actually working for us that obliterate these models. So they take the safeguards off so you can do much more with them than you can do with the U.S. models. So they're more capable. You trick people into thinking,
turns.zh: 好的。假设中国有些人是那样想的。有什么能比说「让美国 AI 实验室做所有艰苦工作，我们复制他们的模型，我们开源它们」更聪明的策略？我们还有人实际上为我们工作来「改良」这些模型——他们把安全防护（safeguards）去掉，这样你能用它们做的事比用美国模型多得多。所以它们更有能力。你骗人们以为，

turns.en: well, we'll run it on our own hardware and we're airgap it. So it's not going to send anything back to China. But what you didn't know is that it has a zero day hack in it. We're on some certain date that China has planned in 10 years in advance because China is really good at planning things long term in advance. There's a day when everybody's AI that they got for free blows up and stops working and creates a crisis. And that just happens to be the day that they launched the
turns.zh: 嗯，我们在自己的硬件上运行而且气隔了，所以它不会向中国回传任何东西。但你不知道的是它里面有一个零日漏洞（zero day hack）。在中国提前十年计划的某个日期——因为中国真的非常擅长长期规划——有一天所有人免费获得的 AI 会爆炸、停止工作并制造一场危机。而那一天恰好就是他们发动

turns.en: military offensive. I mean, there's so many ways, and I'm making up science fiction. I'm certainly not suggesting, oh, this is what's happening. I'm just saying there's so many possibilities here.
turns.zh: 军事进攻的日子。我是说有太多可能性了——我在编科幻故事。我当然不是在暗示「哦这就是正在发生的事」。我只是说这里有太多可能性了。

turns.en: We have no idea what's going on. And I think the idea of an arms limitation negotiation with China to say, let's not go to war over AI models. Let's not make that the next nuclear weapon.
turns.zh: 我们不知道正在发生什么。而且我认为与中国进行军备限制谈判的想法——说「我们不要因 AI 模型开战，不要让它成为下一件核武器」——

turns.en: It seems like kind of a good idea to me. Again, in principle, yes. I'm just saying in reality, history suggests that isn't going to happen. And what terrifies me just as much as the science fiction stories you're telling is that large parts of the U.S., and I've already mentioned cutting edge universities in science, et cetera, and Wall Street, their attitude is, brah, what about next quarter? What about results? And how you can square, because markets as a philosophy
turns.zh: 在我看来这是个好主意。同样，原则上是的。我只是说在现实中，历史表明那不会发生。让我同样恐惧的——就像你讲的那些科幻故事一样——是美国的大部分人，我已经提到了前沿大学在科学等方面，以及 Wall Street，他们的态度是「兄弟，下个季度怎么办？业绩怎么办？」你怎么能把「因为市场」作为一种哲学

turns.en: versus the tail risk of that kind of national security threat, it ludes me above and beyond the fact that there's a died in the wall, almost religious ideology at play, which is somehow everything works out okay if I make money next quarter. And I work in financial markets.
turns.zh: 与那种国家安全威胁的尾部风险调和起来？这让我困惑。不仅如此，还存在一种根深蒂固的、几乎是宗教性的意识形态——不知怎的如果我下个季度赚了钱，一切都会好。而我在金融市场工作。

turns.en: My financial markets are essential for pricing things and to avoiding long run expensive mistakes in the allocation of capital. So I completely understand why we have them. I do not understand why we think that they will continue to operate as untrammeled and freely as they do now when we see door after door being slammed in our faces and window after window being slammed shut.
turns.zh: 我的金融市场对于定价和避免资本配置中的长期昂贵错误是必不可少的。所以我完全理解为什么我们有它们。我不理解的是为什么我们认为它们会继续像现在这样不受约束地自由运作——当我们看到一扇又一扇门在我们面前被砰然关上，一扇又一扇窗被关闭。

turns.en: I'm sure there are many more doors and windows to be shut yet. When you talk about doors and windows to be shut, do you mean things like capital controls that suddenly lock? You know, you got your investments all over the world. And guess what? Now you don't need more because you can't repatriate them because they change the rules. Is that the kind of thing you foresee? That's already happening. It's happening in slow motion and it's happening
turns.zh: 我确信还有更多的门窗要被关闭。当你说门窗要被关闭时，你是指像资本管制（capital controls）那样突然锁死的事情吗？你知道的，你的投资遍布全世界。然后猜猜怎么着？现在你完蛋了因为你不能把它们汇回来——因为他们改了规则。那是你预见的那种情况吗？那已经在发生了。它以慢动作的方式在发生，而且以

turns.en: at a rate where you could anticipate it and get out of the way before it happens. It's not overrunning anyone and catching them off guard yet. No, not yet. Not yet. But then once it's caught you off guard, you're too late. But I mean, there are many jurisdictions where you already have ruinously high exit taxes. Then talking about a couple of them are bringing in unrealized capital gains taxes as well. So we're going to tax you every year on what we think that's worth,
turns.zh: 一种你可以预见到并在它发生之前让开的速度在发生。它还没有超越任何人或让人措手不及。是的，还没有。还没有。但一旦被打了个措手不及，你就太晚了。但我指的是有很多司法管辖区已经有了高得离谱的退出税（exit taxes）。然后其中几个还在引入未实现资本利得税（unrealized capital gains taxes）。所以我们要每年对你认为值多少钱来征税，

turns.en: even if you haven't actually sold it. It's just you have to pay us every year. And if you leave, yeah, half of what you have to stay with us. There are more and more countries bringing that in.
turns.zh: 即使你实际上没有卖掉它。就是你每年必须付钱给我们。而且如果你离开，是的，你的一半财产要留给我们。越来越多的国家在引入这种做法。

turns.en: And I expect that to be extended and extended because governments are so cash trapped everywhere. Now, is that a capital control? No, that's just pretty high taxation. But for people who have significant capital to invest is something to consider. But I do think, again, we are not going to be able to live in a world where national security is to the fore, where key commodities like energy and diesel are being thought over in zero sum contexts. And we're at the same time,
turns.zh: 我预计这会不断扩展，因为各国政府到处都现金紧缺。那这是资本管制吗？不，那只是相当高的税收。但对于有大量资本可投资的人来说是需要考虑的。但我确实认为，同样，我们将无法生活在一个国家安全放在首位的世界里——关键商品如能源和柴油在零和语境中被思考——同时

turns.en: you say, well, you can move your money wherever you want at the click of a button and we don't care where you put it. That does not make any sense at all when governments are cash trapped and looking for funds to fuel what will be necessary in terms of AI infrastructure, if you don't have any, and most countries don't, or defense infrastructure, which most countries don't have enough of, or energy and key commodity stockpiles, which most countries don't have enough
turns.zh: 你说，嗯，你可以在点击一个按钮时把钱转到任何你想去的地方，我们不在乎你放在哪里。当政府现金紧缺、在寻找资金来资助 AI 基础设施（如果你没有的话——大多数国家没有）、或国防基础设施（大多数国家没有足够的）、或能源和关键商品储备（大多数国家没有足够的）时，这完全说不通。

turns.en: of. It's going to cost a lot of money. How are you going to get it? Make sure the money doesn't go wherever people want it to go, but goes towards the social or political good that you think takes priority. And I'm not saying this is a happy outcome. And I'm not saying this is something that's going to have me lying in bed peacefully at night rather than tossing and turning.
turns.zh: 这将花费大量资金。你怎么筹到？确保资金不会流向人们想让它去的地方，而是流向你认为优先的社会或政治利益。我不是在说这是一个令人愉快的结果。我也不是在说这会让我晚上安然入睡而不是辗转反侧。

turns.en: I'm just saying that history shows you that's the overwhelming likelihood. And we are seeing more and more elements of that emerging already. And just those headlines that we have just discussed just in this part two, more than enough evidence to me to say that I expect that process to accelerate going forward rather than slow down. Michael, final topic. It was an awkward moment in part one.
turns.zh: 我只是说历史表明这是压倒性的可能。而且我们已经看到越来越多的元素在浮现。仅在我们刚刚讨论的这第二部分的那些标题中，就有足够的证据让我说我预计这个过程会加速而不是放缓。Michael，最后一个话题。在第一部分有一个尴尬的时刻。

turns.en: I started to allude and didn't say the word first strike nuclear offensive. It is possible, and we certainly have several US politicians, including Lindsey Graham, openly calling for the US to make a first nuclear strike against Iran. When I started to allude to that, you kind of said, well, I think I know what you're talking about. Why are both of us afraid to say something that's in the news that elected officials in the United States are openly advocating
turns.zh: 我开始暗示但没有说出「先发制人核打击」（first strike nuclear offensive）这个词。这确实是可能的，而且我们确实有好几位美国政客——包括 Lindsey Graham——公开呼吁美国对伊朗进行首次核打击。当我开始暗示那个时，你有点说「嗯，我想我知道你在说什么」。为什么我们俩都害怕说出一个已经在新闻中的、美国民选官员公开主张的东西——

turns.en: is if it's taboo. Why are we both afraid to say this on a podcast? Well, I think to an extent excuse the black humor because people don't like thinking about following Lindsey Graham, of course, he's no longer with us. But I would say that it is a very uncomfortable topic, but you are quite correct. It is mentioned even in mainstream press on the front pages. And what I will say is going back to that now,
turns.zh: 如果它是禁忌的话。为什么我们俩都害怕在播客上说这个？嗯，我想在某种程度上——请原谅这种黑色幽默——因为人们不喜欢思考这个。说到 Lindsey Graham，当然他已经不在了。但我要说这确实是一个非常不舒服的话题，但你完全正确。即使在主流媒体头版也有提及。我要说的是回到那个话题——

turns.en: and let's use the terminology. I don't actually think we are heading for a nuclear war. I want to be abundantly clear because people sometimes listen to what I'm saying. They listen to me talking about economic statecraft and realpolitik. And they think they see mushroom clouds, the complete opposite. That's the very last thing that I think anybody rationally wants.
turns.zh: 让我们使用这个术语。我实际上不认为我们正在走向核战争。我要非常清楚地说明，因为人们有时听我说的话——他们听我谈论经济治国术（economic statecraft）和现实政治（realpolitik）——然后他们看到了蘑菇云。恰恰相反。那是我认为任何理性的人最不想要的东西。

turns.en: And everything else I'm talking about is a way to avoid that. But, and here's a big caveat, but there can be situations and it's possible the Middle East is one emerging, whereby the foe that you are dealing with, and here is the Iranians, are so entrenched, so capable of causing absolute chaos along supply chains, that the strategy that you would like to employ, which is let's keep the Middle East destabilized in order to make sure that something bad doesn't happen next year
turns.zh: 我谈论的所有其他东西都是为了避免那个。但——这里有一个很大的但是——可能存在这样的情景，中东可能正在浮现一个：你面对的对手——这里是伊朗人——如此根深蒂固、如此有能力在供应链上制造绝对混乱，以至于你想采用的策略——即让中东保持不稳定以确保明年在东亚不会发生坏事——

turns.en: in East Asia, is too painful for you to carry. In that case, you have to try and pivot back to your primary objective. Let's flip Iran, like Venezuela, so I'm sitting pretty in terms of that key commodity complex. And one of the only ways that that might happen, particularly in terms of Iran's own nuclear program, which is deep underground, particularly underneath Píkáx mountain in particular, where they may or may not be doing, you know, very nefarious things. The only way you
turns.zh: 对你来说代价太大了。在这种情况下，你必须试图转回到你的首要目标。让我们像翻转委内瑞拉一样翻转伊朗，这样我在关键大宗商品方面就处于有利地位。而唯一可能做到这一点的方式之一——特别是就伊朗自己的核计划而言，它深埋地下——特别是在 Pikax 山下——他们可能在那里做着非常见不得人的事情也可能没有。你唯一

turns.en: might be able to do that is to drop a tactical nuclear weapon or a series of tactical nuclear weapons on them. Now, that opens an absolute Pandora's box.
